Today's data is essentially a level-check, not a signal day: every company across the hyperscaler, chipmaker, and datacenter-infrastructure cohorts shows zero 8-K filings and no percent-change history yet on stock price or volume, meaning there's nothing to compare against 1d/7d/30d baselines. That absence is itself worth noting only insofar as it's uniform — Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta, Nvidia, Broadcom, AMD, TSMC, ASML, Arm, Oracle, Dell, Supermicro, CoreWeave, Digital Realty, Equinix, Vertiv, and Eaton all filed nothing today, which is unremarkable given 8-Ks are lumpy, low-frequency events rather than a daily cadence — a quiet day across eighteen names doesn't imply synchronized caution, just an ordinary non-filing day.

On raw levels, Nvidia's volume stands out at roughly 48.9 million shares versus single-digit-million to low-teens-million for most peers, and Oracle's ~18.2 million and Amazon's ~17.7 million are elevated relative to the quieter infrastructure names like Equinix (~229K) and Digital Realty (~765K) — but without prior-period deltas this is just a snapshot of typical liquidity differences between mega-caps and REIT-structured datacenter plays, not evidence of a move.

The open-source ML repo activity is the only category with standalone current values worth noting as context: PyTorch (76 commits) and vLLM (70 commits) are seeing heavy daily commit volume versus DeepSpeed (10) and Hugging Face Transformers (7), consistent with where community development energy currently concentrates, though a single day's commit count is noisy and shouldn't be read as a trend absent history.

Only one-day deltas are populated today (no 7d/30d history yet), so this is a snapshot rather than a trend read — worth flagging up front given the usual caution about over-reading single-day moves, especially on low-volume series.

The standout equity move is a broad-based rally across the physical AI-infrastructure and power/cooling names: Digital Realty (+3.0%), Vertiv (+2.9%), CoreWeave (+2.9%), Eaton (+2.4%), Equinix (+2.8%), and Dell (+2.7%) all posted gains of roughly 2.5-3%, notably outpacing the hyperscalers and chipmakers. AMD (+3.5%) was the single biggest mover of the day, alongside modest gains at Nvidia (+1.9%) and Arm (+1.6%). Meanwhile Microsoft (-1.1%) and Amazon (-0.3%) were the only names in the red. No company filed an 8-K today — across all sixteen tickers — so there's no fresh capex-disclosure signal to weigh against the price action.

The clearest cross-company pattern is that data-center/power-and-cooling infrastructure stocks (DLR, VRT, EQIX, ETN) moved together and in the same direction as compute names like CRWV and DELL, suggesting the market's enthusiasm today was concentrated in physical AI buildout exposure rather than the software/model layer. Every metric in today's pull is stock price/volume and a handful of GitHub commit counts — no hiring, capex-signal, or utilization data came through, so this is a narrower read than usual, essentially a one-day market-reaction snapshot rather than a fundamentals update.

That said, the day's price action was unusually synchronized across the AI-infrastructure hardware and datacenter-buildout complex. ARM (+6.9%), SMCI (+10.4%), AMD (+5.0%), ORCL (+4.2%), DELL (+4.1%), and AVGO (+2.6%) all rallied together, and the volume behind those moves was extreme rather than incidental: SMCI volume was up 222.6%, ARM up 178.3%, AMD up 48.7%, and ETN (grid/power equipment) up 94.3% even as its price only rose 2.5%. That combination — broad-based gains across chipmakers, server OEMs, and power-equipment names on sharply elevated volume — looks like a real, coordinated market re-rating of the AI-capex trade for the day, worth noting as a shared move even though the dashboard can't say what triggered it. CRWV was the outlier, falling 5.3% on a 423.5% volume spike and filing an 8-K same-day, which given the size of the volume move deserves watching but isn't yet enough to characterize beyond "something happened."

On the software side, the commit data is thin and one 300% jump (DeepSpeed, 2→8 commits) is just noise from a low base, not signal. Today is a broad, one-directional risk-off day across the entire AI-infrastructure complex, with only one-day data available for essentially every metric — so treat this as a snapshot of sentiment, not a trend. Every name in the dataset fell except CRWV, which rose 4.8% on volume that actually collapsed 63.1%, an odd pairing worth flagging but not leaning on. The steepest declines came from the chip and hardware layer: ARM dropped 7.4%, AMD fell 6.5%, SMCI slid 9.3%, and ORCL and DELL each lost roughly 4%. Volume tells the more interesting story than price here — MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, AVGO, TSM, and DELL all saw trading volume roughly double (107-124% above baseline), while DLR and EQIX, the two datacenter REITs, saw volume spike far more violently (+696% and +353% respectively) despite comparatively modest price moves of -1.5% and -0.9%. That combination — muted price, extreme volume — suggests repositioning or index-related flow in the physical-infrastructure names rather than a fundamental repricing.

The clearest cross-company pattern is the volume surge itself: it's not confined to one sub-sector but spans hyperscalers (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META), foundry/chip (TSM, AVGO), and enterprise hardware (DELL, ORCL) simultaneously, which points to a market-wide event rather than company-specific news, though nothing in this dataset identifies what that catalyst was. SMCI and ARM stand out as the two names where price damage outpaced the volume story, suggesting idiosyncratic selling on top of the broader move.
